text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- A conflict of interests drives a wedge between former allies in the top management of the Krasnoyarsk aluminium smelter.
- First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais has managed to get his economic policy message through to the deputies of the upper chamber of parliament.
- A simmering conflict between Moscow and the governor of the Primorsky region in Russia's Far East could burst into an open clash any time.
- Anatoly Chubais drives a Suzuki off-road vehicle, according to his official declaration on income and property.
- The World Bank has granted six new credits to Russia in one go.
- A crisis management team has started work at the Magnitogorsk steel mill.
- The shareholders' meeting at the aircraft engine producer Perm Motors appoints a new director general to drive the plant out of a deep crisis.
- Russia will have a unified market for regional bonds.
- Yeilds on state securities continue to fall.
- St Petersburg has managed to place its bonds on the world market on better terms than Moscow did some time ago.
SEVODNYA
- Russia is still planning to buy from Kiev ultra-long range strategic bombers left on Ukrainian territory after the break-up of the Soviet Union.
- Reformers in the government seem to place their bets on regional bosses to push forward reforms.
- Customs officials will now have to taste and test all wines to be imported into Russia.
- The World Bank is starting a new series of credits to Russia aimed at providing conditions for sustainable development of the economy.
- Aeroflot is offering rock-bottom air tariffs to all destinations for a limited period this summer.
- The auction to sell off a 25 percent stake in the telecommunications giant Svyazinvest has been postponed once again.
- Moscow securities exchange will start dealing in companies' shares in July.
- Moscow property developers mull stepping over the outer ring road and into the neighbouring region in search of profits.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov urges Japanese businessmen to invest in Russia but his rapturous outlook on the country's economy may be far from reality.
- The Russian budget has funds earmarked for Chechnya and money transfers could start as soon as President Boris Yeltsin gives the go-ahead.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- Primorsky region governor Yevgeny Nazdratenko is leading his territory up a blind alley.
- Anatoly Chubais points out at a meeting with the Federation Council upper house of parliament that state regulation of the economy should be balanced and accurate.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS

- Senators in Russia's Federation Council have given a warm welcome to Anatoly Chubais's assessment of today's state of economy, leaving unnoticed many deficiencies in the government's economic management.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
